title: Add Private deployment example: audit log export + KMS configuration
author: Fatima Noor
description:
Context: During regulated workload deep dives (ABM pilot), multiple prospects asked for a concrete “show me” reference of (a) what audit log export configuration looks like in Redwood Private deployments and (b) how KMS-backed envelope encryption settings are wired for log payloads + secrets. This PR adds a small, intentionally minimal example under redwood-examples that SEs can share during technical sessions and point to when answering questionnaire-style questions (export format, fields, delivery to SIEM, and KMS key usage). Scope: Example only (no product changes). Includes a sample config (values.yaml-style) and a tiny exporter that tails the audit log stream and ships JSONL to either S3 (assume role) or an HTTPS collector. Notes: 1) No claim of compliance certification; README includes “reference only” disclaimer. 2) Audit fields match current docs (ENG-22091 verification). 3) KMS config is documented as optional; on-prem deployments may use customer HSM/KMS-compatible endpoints.

What’s included: - examples/private-deployments/audit-log-export/README.md (setup, threat model notes, and how to validate) - config/private-values.example.yaml (audit logging + retention + export destination knobs) - exporter/export_audit_logs.py (reference exporter; supports S3 + HTTP) - exporter/requirements.txt - scripts/generate_sample_events.py (for demo/testing) - .github/workflows/examples-auditlog-ci.yml (lint + basic run)

Illustrative snippet (from private-values.example.yaml): audit_logging: enabled: true level: "INFO" include_request_metadata: true redact: pii: true secrets: true export: enabled: true format: "jsonl" destination: type: "s3" bucket: "<customer-audit-bucket>" prefix: "redwood/audit/" region: "us-east-1" kms: key_arn: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:<acct>:key/<uuid>" sse: "aws:kms" buffering: max_bytes: 5242880 max_seconds: 10

Security notes included in README: - Exporter uses least-privileged IAM (PutObject only to prefix) - Recommends separate KMS key for audit logs vs runtime secrets - Provides guidance on log integrity controls (object lock / immutability) but does not claim it is enabled by default - Clarifies that retention is customer-configured and must be aligned with internal policy

Requested follow-ups (out of scope for this PR): - Add a Terraform module for the S3 + KMS + IAM setup (tracked in a separate issue) - Add a schema doc that enumerates all audit fields with examples (Docs is handling via regulated FAQ updates)

Screenshots: N/A (CLI-only example).
commits: examples(private): add audit log export reference directory + README
examples(security): document KMS settings and least-privilege IAM policy
ci: add workflow to run exporter in dry-run mode + ruff formatting
fix: align sample audit event keys with current audit schema (ENG-22091)
review_conversation:
Markus Klein (review): “This is great for the Regal Wealth-style questions. Two asks: (1) make it explicit that the exporter is reference-only and not supported as a product feature, and (2) include a section on ‘what fields are in the audit event’ with at least one full example payload.”

Fatima Noor (author): “Good call. Added a disclaimer up top + added a full payload example with notes on which fields may be omitted depending on policy (e.g., request metadata toggles).”

Naomi Feldman (review): “Please avoid wording that sounds like we provide immutable logs by default. Also, ensure the KMS section doesn’t imply we manage customer keys. Can you add ‘customer-managed KMS/HSM’ language and explicitly note that key policies are owned by the customer?”

Fatima Noor (author): “Updated: replaced ‘immutable’ with ‘supports customer-configured immutability (e.g., S3 Object Lock)’ and clarified customer-managed KMS/HSM + key policy ownership.”

Kira Thompson (review): “Config naming: we’ve been using `audit_logging.export.format` in docs; this example uses `format` but also introduces `buffering`. Can we annotate buffering as exporter-only, not a platform knob, to avoid confusion?”

Fatima Noor (author): “Adjusted README to label buffering settings as exporter implementation details. Left YAML as-is but added comments and moved buffering under exporter-specific section.”

Elliot Price (review): “Minor: add a note on where this should be linked from (regulated landing page / security FAQ). Also please pin the boto3 version to avoid surprise breakage.”

Fatima Noor (author): “Pinned boto3 and added ‘Where to use this’ section with suggested links for SEs and Docs.”

Approvals: Markus Klein approved; Naomi Feldman approved; Kira Thompson approved; Elliot Price approved.
release_notes: Added a reference example for Redwood Private deployments showing audit log export configuration patterns and customer-managed KMS settings for regulated technical deep dives.
